land.text: the northern four-elevenths of the island (about 36% of Cyprus's total area) taken by Turkish forces in 1974

predecessors.note: The Republic of Cyprus (a Cliopatria row, not a dossier of this group) keeps the claim: the UN treats the north as Cypriot territory under Turkish military occupation (Northern Cyprus page).

correction.text: the northern four-elevenths of Cyprus (about 36%) held by Turkish forces after the second phase of the invasion in August 1974, the ground of the Autonomous Turkish Cypriot Administration and then the Turkish Federated State of Cyprus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first row begins in 1976, but the page has Turkey holding 'approximately 36%' of the island after the second phase (14 August 1974) and 'The ceasefire line from August 1974 became the United Nations Buffer Zone', so the same outline holds from August 1974; the 1974-75 shape is therefore the 1976 shape unchanged.

4,341 km2 against the infobox 3,355 km2 (ratio 1.29, within a factor of two). The Cliopatria shape is tagged with 'Cyprus No Mans Area' and 'Cyprus', so it takes in part of the UN buffer zone along the Green Line (page: 'A buffer zone controlled by the UN forms a barrier between both sides of the island'). The page names no border change after 1974 (it is silent on Varosha, Pyla and the crossings' land), so the outline stands for 1976-2023.
Same outline and area (4,341 km2) as 1976-2023; the page records no territorial change.

region.text: the northern four-elevenths of the island (about 36% of Cyprus's total area)

ledger.note: 1974: the Turkish invasion leaves the north under a Turkish Cypriot administration. 'The invasion led to the formation of the first sovereign administrative body of Northern Cyprus in August 1974' and Turkish forces 'proceeded to take over the northern four-elevenths of the island (about 36% of Cyprus's total area)'. The infobox gives 1 October 1974 for the Autonomous Turkish Cypriot Administration, so the page disagrees with itself; August is the body text's. The Turkey-versus-Cyprus fighting of 20 July to August 1974 is in the Republic of Cyprus and Turkey dossiers (counterpart republic-of-turkey there).

1975: the Turkish Federated State of Cyprus is declared on 13 February. Infobox 'Turkish Federated State of Cyprus: 13 February 1975'; 'declared as a first step towards a future federated Cypriot state' (the Turkish invasion page: 'On 13 February 1975, Turkey declared the occupied areas of the Republic of Cyprus to be a "Federated Turkish State"'). The land is unchanged.

region.text: the occupied areas of the Republic of Cyprus, declared by Turkey on 13 February 1975 to be a "Federated Turkish State"

ledger.note: 13 February 1975: 'Turkey declared the occupied areas of the Republic of Cyprus to be a "Federated Turkish State"' (reopened 2026-11-01); the same page says of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus 'Turkey is the only country that recognises it'. Mirror of republic-of-turkey ledger/6 (1975-02 vassal_start, counterpart turkish-republic-of-northern-cyprus, same Cliopatria 1976 shape), added after review. No vassal_end: the relation lasts to the end of this dossier (2026). Confidence 2 because the page says what Turkey declared, not what the legal tie was, and the north's own sovereignty claim (rename of 15 November 1983) is a separate event.

1983: the north declares itself the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus on 15 November. 'The north unilaterally declared its independence on 15 November 1983'; recognised only by Turkey. The Turkish invasion page adds that UN Security Council Resolution 541 'considers the declaration referred to above as legally invalid'. The land is unchanged.

wars.name: Turkish invasion of Cyprus

zones.text: the northern four-elevenths of Cyprus (about 36%) captured in two phases

wars.outcome: Turkey took about 3% of the island in the first phase (20-22 July 1974) and 'approximately 36%' after the second (from 14 August); the August 1974 ceasefire line became the UN Buffer Zone, with the north under the Turkish Cypriot administration that became this state.
wars.note: The TRNC did not yet exist as a belligerent: the Turkish army fought the Cypriot National Guard, whose coup of 15 July 1974 (led by its Greek officers) triggered the invasion. The fighting zones are drawn as contest in the Republic of Cyprus and Turkey dossiers; this dossier starts when the held ground becomes an administration.

certainty.note: A de facto ceasefire line (August 1974) now the UN Buffer Zone, not a treaty frontier: the Republic of Cyprus and the UN treat the whole island as Cypriot territory. The line is fixed and patrolled, so it is drawn sharp.

notes: One dossier for the Cliopatria row 'Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus' (1976..2024, 2 shapes, both the same 4,341 km2 outline). Dossier start is August 1974 (page: administration formed 'in August 1974'; infobox says 1 October 1974), two years before Cliopatria's 1976, so one new keyframe covers 1974-75. A 1974 'found' event stands in for the gain from republic-of-cyprus; no separate contest events are written here because the combatant of July-August 1974 was Turkey (the Republic of Cyprus dossier already has contest_start/contest_end and occupation_start against republic-of-turkey for the same northern zone, with no occupation_end). Needs attention from the orchestrator: (1) the north is drawn there as Turkish occupation and here as a state of its own; the Turkey dossier (me-10, republic-of-turkey ledger/6) already has a vassal_start of 1975-02 with counterpart 'turkish-republic-of-northern-cyprus', so this dossier now carries the mirror (ledger/2, vassal_start, counterpart 'republic-of-turkey', no vassal_end because the relation lasts to 2026); from August 1974 to February 1975 the north is Turkish occupation (republic-of-cyprus and republic-of-turkey ledgers, no occupation_end there), and the colour agent decides whether the later vassal tint replaces or overlays the hatching. (2) The population exchange of 2 August 1975 ('196,000 Greek Cypriots living in the north were exchanged for 42,000 Turkish Cypriots living in the south') moved people, not borders, and has no event type. (3) Pages silent: Varosha/Maras, Pyla, the 2003-04 crossings' dates, the first president, any ruler list (no rulers written). (4) 2004: Annan Plan referendum, '65% of Turkish Cypriots accepted ... 76% of Greek Cypriots rejected it' (April 2004): no border change. Page budget (1-2 pages) spent on 2 pages. Region names used: 'Northern Cyprus' (country) resolves in the gazetteer; nothing missing.
